label: proposed next experiments (proposals only; none run)

experiments.title: Exposure-matched sequencing test (fix the staging experiment's main confound)
experiments.question: After equalising cumulative exposure to the education-share and vacancy-rate changes, does the school-first vs jobs-first difference in completion/formal-share persist, or was it a cumulative-dose artefact?
experiments.design: eduengine formal_loop with 6 arms: none; school_first; jobs_first; simultaneous; school_first_matched; jobs_first_matched. Matched arms deliver the SAME total education-share-years and vacancy-years as their counterpart (e.g. shorten the early period or compensate late), so only ORDER differs. Add a calendar-shift placebo (both events shifted +10 years, same order) to separate calendar/cohort-window effects. 6 arms x 2 feedback x 2 gates x 20 seeds = 480 runs; pre-declare all contrasts and the exposure arithmetic (audited: unmatched arms differ by +1.8 edu-share-years / -1.2 vacancy-years).
experiments.falsifier: If the matched order contrast is ~0 while the unmatched contrast is large, the original 'timing effect' is cumulative exposure, not sequencing. If the matched contrast keeps the sign and clears its seed bootstrap CI, order has a model-internal effect worth following up in a more structural design.
experiments.splits: None needed (synthetic); report all arms and seeds, no selection; seed bootstrap CIs over 20 seeds.
experiments.cost_estimate: 480 runs x ~0.83 CPU-s = ~400 CPU-s; ~30 s wall on 24-48 workers; <5 min end-to-end with monitoring.
experiments.blocked_by: none; only the audited staging harness needs a small extension (new arm definitions), not a new engine.

experiments.title: Gate/quota x shadow-tutoring inequality factorial
experiments.question: Do quota gates (planned seats) versus absolute bar gates change tutoring use and completion differently across household income quintiles and rural/urban location, in the direction the MASSENG account predicts?
experiments.design: eduengine: gates bar vs quota x tutoring access (rural_firm_access 0.2/0.4/0.8) x own-teacher ban (0/enforced) x 20 seeds = 240 runs; outcomes by level and wealth quintile: completion, tut_rate, tut_by_q, parity_wealth/location; pre-declare directional expectations (quota gates -> more gate-prep tutoring; richer/urban households capture more).
experiments.falsifier: Pre-declared: if quota gates do not raise gate-prep tutoring relative to bar gates (sign and CI), or do not widen the top-vs-bottom tutoring gap, the model's gate/tutoring channel does not produce the claimed pattern (conditional on the rest of the design).
experiments.splits: None (synthetic); all cells reported; no post-hoc subgroup selection.
experiments.cost_estimate: 240 runs x ~0.83 CPU-s = ~200 CPU-s; <1 min wall on 24 workers.

experiments.title: Education-to-jobs feedback-elasticity robustness surface
experiments.question: Are any sequencing conclusions robust to the assumed education-to-jobs feedback (job_elasticity)?
experiments.design: eduengine: job_elasticity in {0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0} x 4 schedules x 2 gates x 20 seeds = 800 runs; report the full contrast surface with seed bootstrap CIs; pre-declare that conclusions must be stable across the whole elasticity range (or be reported as conditional).
experiments.falsifier: Any order conclusion that reverses sign across the elasticity grid is not robust; report the reversal and do not select the elasticity that gives the preferred answer.
experiments.cost_estimate: 800 runs x ~0.83 CPU-s = ~660 CPU-s; ~1-2 min wall on 24-48 workers.

experiments.title: Observed-data staging/ordering test with honest splits (aggregate level only)
experiments.question: Where the observed panels allow, does a pre-declared model-implied timing/ordering score predict held-out changes in enrolment/completion better than persistence or trend benchmarks?
experiments.design: Use committed WDI/UIS panel (pre_ger, prm_ner, sec_ner, lsc), transition onset dates, and (if used) child_work only as a sparse secondary outcome. Freeze: train on countries/periods disjoint from validation (e.g. leave-country-out blocks and pre-1996 -> 1996-2015); pre-register the ordering score and the benchmark losses. Report absolute losses and paired predictive differences with country-cluster bootstrap CIs. No new data pull; no DHS microdata.
experiments.falsifier: If the model-implied ordering score does not beat persistence and trend on held-out countries (paired differences with CIs), the observed data do not support the staging prediction at this aggregate; report it as such.
experiments.splits: Pre-registered leave-country-out + time-block split; no Q2/E1 observation reused across splits; if too few countries, report insufficient evidence.
experiments.cost_estimate: panel regressions only; minutes of CPU (no simulation).
experiments.blocked_by: construct mismatch: only aggregate enrolment/completion, no child-work states or tutoring; results would be exploratory and cannot identify mechanisms.

experiments.title: Bayesian screen validation and synthetic parameter recovery (coordinate with Lead/Codex)
experiments.question: Are the v5 R1 importance screens usable at all: do they recover known parameters, pass ESS/weight diagnostics, and stay stable across seeds, priors and tolerance?
experiments.design: Use existing run_screen.py (no model edits): (i) synthetic recovery - simulate from known b_h,b_p,b_r,lam draws and check coverage/bias; (ii) weight diagnostics - max weight share, ESS, degenerate draws; (iii) seed stability - >=2 seeds per prior; (iv) prior and tolerance sensitivity; (v) posterior-predictive coverage vs persistence/trend benchmarks. Report everything; no posterior claim.
experiments.falsifier: If synthetic recovery fails (coverage far below nominal / parameters unidentifiable) or ESS remains very low at the declared budget, the screens are not usable and no posterior/mechanism claim can be made.
experiments.splits: Synthetic known-parameter recovery + committed/active screen outputs; no observed holdout claims (post-1995 already inspected).
experiments.data: D12 (v5 R1 fit), existing screen code
experiments.cost_estimate: needs one measured 4,096-draw screen wall first (active runs); budget <=1 h server time for recovery+diagnostics at 24 workers; do not promise draw counts before the timing measure.
experiments.blocked_by: active 4,096-draw screens must complete/be owned by Lead; do not duplicate.
